content_html:
Extra rinse adds another water phase to remove more detergent and suspended soil after washing. It can help with very dirty loads, fabrics that retain product, or people sensitive to residue, but it should not become a permanent workaround for overdosing detergent or overloading the washer.

It adds water after the main wash

The washer fills, moves the load, and drains again to carry away remaining product. It does not add more detergent or increase the original wash action.

It can help when real residue remains

If thick items come out soapy or an unusually dirty load required more product within the allowed dose, an extra rinse can improve the result.

It does not fix chronic detergent overdose

If every load needs an extra rinse, reduce the dose and review concentration, water hardness, and load size. Using more water every wash is not the best solution to incorrect dosing.

It also increases water use and cycle time

Use it when it provides a specific benefit rather than by default. Some cycles or machines already adjust rinsing automatically based on suds or load conditions.
